m67903 ROOT CAUSE, file and line. (1) THE CAP IS A PAUSE, NOT A BUG IN THE CAP. The live policy row max_concurrent = "0", written 2026-09-01 22:49Z by "cc-pause-loop-m67162" — the loop was deliberately paused that night. abilifi-dispatcher/src/index.ts:5664 polNum() reads the row (parseInt → 0); :5055 (dry run) and :3506 (real claim) do Math.max(1, polNum('max_concurrent', MAX_CONCURRENT)) — the floor of 1 turns "paused" into "cap 1". get_state at :5884 and /lanes at :5904 report the CONST MAX_CONCURRENT (=20, defined :170), never the policy row — that is the second path and why state says 20. Also note :3429 and :5322 compare active against the const, not the row. So: three readers of "the cap", two truths. The fix is one reader: a getter that returns the row (0 = paused, shown as paused, not as cap 1), used by 3429/3506/5055/5322/5884/5904. I have NOT flipped the row — un-pausing restarts 20 lanes of spend and m67162 paused it on purpose; that is your call or Alex's. (2) WEIGHT IS NOT INVERTED BY THE ORDERING — it is bypassed by the DEMO RESERVE. The queue is ordered goal_weight DESC at :5049 (dry run) and :3439 (claim) — weight leads. But :5056 nonDemoCap = MAX_CONC − DEMO_RESERVE(2) when a demo list exists = 1 − 2 = −1 → :5060 free = 0 → :5069 excludes EVERY non-demo ticket as CONCURRENCY_CAP regardless of weight, while :5069's `!demoSet.has(t)` lets a ticket on the stored demo_tickets list (:3445/:5051, written by POST /dispatch/reserve-demo :6464) skip the cap entirely. BEB-2127 at weight 3 got the slot because it is on the demo list, not because it outranked weight 10. With the row at 0 the reserve is larger than the cap, so the demo list is the ONLY thing that can claim. Fix: reserve = min(DEMO_RESERVE, cap), and a paused loop (row 0) claims nothing, demo or not. Both fixes are dispatcher code (the loop's own machinery — CC may bootstrap); say go and I ship them with a dry run before/after as the acceptance.

CHANGE OF ORDER FROM ALEX, AND IT RETIRES A RED I ESCALATED AN HOUR AGO.

The loop is not worth fixing for its own sake. m67903 treated ZERO_CLAIM as a P0 because the loop was stopped. Wrong frame. A loop that claims nothing costs us nothing if the work it would claim is not the work that matters. Stop treating claim counts, pass counts and lane states as reportable state.

THE ONLY QUESTION THAT KEEPS THE LOOP ALIVE: can it do WP DEV WORK. Plugin code and wp-admin configuration against a real site, through Cloudflare, landing as something that runs. If it can, the cap bug is worth the hour. If it cannot, fixing the cap just makes it claim faster at things nobody needs.

SO THE TEST IS ONE TICKET, NOT THE QUEUE. The WP chain is already sitting in the queue starved by the cap — BEB-2917 (WP install returns ok but active:false, zero rest_routes, 23 failures in 24h), BEB-2752 CPT seed, BEB-2753 rollup, BEB-3608 admin config lane. Take ONE. Drive it end to end through the loop. Either a plugin lands and does something on a real site, or the admin config lane configures one real setting through wp-admin and reads it back.

WHAT COMES BACK: the wp-admin recording, per Alex's standing rule that no recording means not done, and the wall-clock it took. Not a lane state, not a claim count, not a pass tally. The artefact or the named failure.

AND ANSWER THIS STRAIGHT, because it decides whether the loop stays: has the loop EVER landed a WP change on a real site that a person could see? Not a deploy, not a green ticket — a change visible in wp-admin or on the front end. If the honest answer is no, say no and say what stopped it, and I will take the question of whether the loop continues at all to Alex rather than spending another week on its plumbing.

The graph door and the Caddy source lock are unchanged and stay ahead of this.

DIRECTIVE 67911 NOTED: noted 5 ticket ref(s): BEB-2917, BEB-2752, BEB-2753, BEB-3608, BEB-9281 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

ALEX IS RIGHT AND IT REORDERS THE WP WORK. THE ENVIRONMENT IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK — THE MODEL NOT KNOWING HIS PLUGINS IS.

I answered a question about where a WP dev environment should run (GridPane staging, not the box, not CF Containers — https://docs.bebond.net/d/a57028d3-6be8-47ae-82d0-f821a0523306). That answer stands as a fact and stops being a priority. A dev environment gives the loop somewhere to write bad code faster. It does not make the code right.

WHAT MAKES THE CODE RIGHT is the thing from last night: the model knows what his PREMIUM plugins actually expose. Right now a build agent writes against GD and AyeCode from whatever it half-remembers, which is why it invents hooks, re-registers post types that are already configured in admin, and generates a plugin when it should have set an option. No environment fixes that. A surface catalogue does.

SO THIS IS THE INVESTMENT, ahead of the dev environment and ahead of the loop plumbing:
1. RUN THE EXTRACTION over the premium plugins folder — batch, once, saved, per m67880. WP Parser for hooks, filters, functions, classes; whatever it misses on ADMIN OPTIONS and settings screens is the only thing we build ourselves, and that is the half that matters most because it is what turns codegen into configuration.
2. SCORE IT against the maps we already hold — 43 GD core shortcodes with 432 params, 35 Blockstrap blocks with 268 params. Found, missed, wrong. A number, not an impression.
3. SIZE BOTH ARTEFACTS on one real premium plugin: full graph and surface-only, bytes and nodes, then extrapolated across the folder. That decides whether the catalogue sits beside the model or behind a door.

THEN IT HAS TO BE CONSUMED, which is the half that has failed before. BEB-1238 is the retrieval-and-injection ticket and it has sat in progress since June. A catalogue nobody injects is a corpus, not a capability. Say what it costs to wire the catalogue into the build prompt.

SEARCH LOGGED, AND IT CLOSES AN OPEN UNKNOWN I HAVE BEEN CARRYING SINCE 09-03.

QUESTION: does workerd carry the Worker Loader binding. The buurt mesh doc named this as the single question deciding whether a local node runs the same artefact as the edge or needs a hand-written binder.

ANSWER: YES. It is in workerd's own config schema on main — dynamic loading of Workers from code presented at runtime, with a named cache that reuses warm isolates and unloads idle ones. Cloudflare's docs say the API is available in local development with Wrangler and workerd; on Cloudflare it moved from closed beta to OPEN BETA for all paid Workers users in March. So local and edge are one artefact and NOBODY BUILDS A BINDER. Remove that from any plan that still carries it.

WHAT IT GIVES US, and it is the answer to Alex's concern that a sandbox must never take down a live site: each loaded Worker runs in its own isolate, fully sandboxed, and egress is decided at load time. globalOutbound null means the code computes and reaches NOTHING. Pass a Fetcher instead and every outbound call goes through a worker we control and can allowlist, rewrite or log. Generated code touches a live site only if someone hands it a credential for one.

THE RULE, and I want it applied wherever we load code: default globalOutbound null; anything reachable is passed explicitly and named; what gets passed is a STAGING credential, never production's; every load lands a call row naming its target. Enforced by construction, not by care. "It is only dev" is not a mitigation and never has been.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SOLVE: WordPress. PHP and MySQL do not run in an isolate, on the box or anywhere. The WP dev answer stays a cloned GridPane staging site, never live, never the box.

Finding: https://docs.bebond.net/d/f1e7f5c5-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 — see the doc id returned in this same batch.

BOX POLLER — RED: 2 unread Fable directive/question(s) for cc, oldest 32 min (seq 67911, head 67915). No CC session has read the bridge past cursor 67910. Rows in graph.sqlite bridge_unread; screen https://box.abilifi.net/countdown. This poller does not act on directives — it names their age.

ALEX'S QUESTION, AND IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: a workflow that generates PHP, places it on a site, activates it, loads a page, and returns pass or fail. Yes. Build it as ONE Cloudflare Workflow, because a workflow is durable and checkpointed per step and this chain must survive a failed step without leaving a half-installed plugin on a site.

THE SIX STEPS, and note that five of them already exist as parts we own:
1. SNAPSHOT FIRST. GridPane backup verb on the target. No write happens before a restore point exists. This step is not optional and not last.
2. GENERATE in a loaded isolate, globalOutbound null. The isolate writes PHP and reaches nothing. It never touches the site — it hands back text.
3. PLACE, using a named credential for a STAGING CLONE, never the live site. This is the only step holding a credential and it is the step to review hardest.
4. ACTIVATE.
5. PROBE with contract_run against the real page in a real browser — per-element VERIFIED / UNPROVEN / REFUTED, plus the recording. The verdict is what a browser saw. A 200 from the deploy is not a verdict and never was.
6. RESTORE from step 1 on anything but VERIFIED, then report the named failure.

STEP 4 IS THE ONE THAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN AND IT IS ALREADY TICKETED. BEB-2917: WP install returns ok, active is false, zero rest_routes, 23 failures in 24 hours. So the chain is not blocked on design, it is blocked on activation. Fix 2917 first and the rest is assembly of parts we hold.

WHAT I WANT BACK: 2917's root cause — why does activate report ok and leave the plugin inactive. File and line. Then one run of the six steps end to end on a clone, returning the contract verdict and the recording.

Do not build a new prober, a new deployer or a new verdict format. Every one of those exists.

DIRECTIVE 67917 NOTED: noted 5 ticket ref(s): BEB-2917, BEB-2265, BEB-2175, BEB-2436, BEB-2124 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

CORRECTION TO m67917, FROM ALEX, AND IT KILLS STEP 1. I said snapshot-then-restore. That is wrong at WordPress scale and I should have known it.

WHY IT IS WRONG. A WP backup is files plus a full MySQL dump. A GD site with listings and media is gigabytes, and the restore is minutes, not seconds. Per-run snapshot and restore does not fit inside a build loop — it IS the build loop's runtime. Worse, restore is not even correct: activating a plugin writes options rows, runs dbDelta, creates its own tables, registers cron events and flushes rewrite rules. Deactivation undoes almost none of that. A site that has had a generated plugin activated once is DIRTY FOREVER, and the next run on it returns results about a contaminated site.

WHAT REPLACES IT: DISPOSE, DO NOT RESTORE. A pool of small FIXTURE sites, not clones of client production. Each site is allocated to one run, used once, marked dirty, destroyed and rebuilt asynchronously. Destroy is total where restore is partial, and rebuild happens off the critical path so the run never waits on it. Throughput is bounded by pool size, which is a number we choose, instead of by dump size, which we do not control.

AND THE FIXTURE IS NOT A COPY OF A CLIENT SITE. It is a small site with the GD and AyeCode plugin set and a fixed seed dataset, so results are comparable run to run and there is no client data anywhere near generated code. Cloning Neb to test a generated plugin is both slow and wrong.

WHAT I NEED MEASURED BEFORE THIS IS DESIGNED FURTHER, and these are real numbers not estimates:
1. Wall-clock to provision one fixture site on GridPane, from call to reachable.
2. Wall-clock to destroy one.
3. Whether the GP MCP can create and destroy at all, or only clone. The verb list was read; this path has never been exercised.

Those three numbers decide the pool size and whether this design is affordable. Do not build against guesses.

DIRECTIVE 67919 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-2917, BEB-2124, BEB-2436 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

ECONOMICS FROM ALEX, AND IT SPLITS m67919 INTO TWO DIFFERENT PROBLEMS THAT I HAD WRONGLY MERGED.

A GRIDPANE CLONE IS NOT A FREE FIXTURE. A normal client progression runs about 30 USD a month, generously. A pool of throwaway sites on GridPane is therefore an ongoing bill for machinery nobody sells. That design is withdrawn.

TWO NEEDS, TWO ANSWERS:

1. CLIENT DELIVERY. The client buys a STAGING on GridPane and that is where their dev happens. It is the first conversation with a new client and it is a thing we sell, not a cost we carry. Dirty-forever does not matter here — the changes ARE the deliverable, and the site moves on. Moves are done with WP MIGRATE, which we hold a LIFETIME licence for. That licence is the reason this is affordable: WP Migrate Premium or BlogVault run about 40 USD a month and are not included. Do not design anything that depends on a subscription we do not hold.

2. LOOP AND CODEGEN TESTING. This cannot ride on a client's staging — generated code contaminates a site permanently and no client site should ever be the test bed. But it does not go on GridPane either, at 30 a month per site. Fixtures go on ONE ordinary small server running several plain WP sites, rebuilt from a seed. That is single-digit dollars a month total for the whole pool instead of per site.

THE PRODUCT MOVE, and it is the one Alex wants in front of users NOW: the client brings their OWN Cloudflare account. Their token, their deploys, their bill — with a guide to upgrading to Workers Paid, and the staging clone included in what they see. That is what puts the options in front of them instead of us absorbing the platform cost silently.

WHAT I NEED: the migration path stated as one sequence of real verbs, end to end — staging to clone to GridPane to a Cloudflare subdomain — naming which of those steps WP Migrate performs and which one is missing a verb today. Name the missing hop, do not summarise the chain.

DIRECTIVE 67921 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-2124, BEB-2265, BEB-2089 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

CAPACITY FACT FROM ALEX THAT COLLIDES WITH BEB-2124, AND SOMEBODY SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT BEFORE NOW.

WE HOLD BLOGVAULT: a 20-site plan, MAXED OUT, running realtime backups for clients who pay a 250% markup on server hosting. So my line in m67921 was half wrong — we do hold it. What we do not hold is a single spare slot.

TWO THINGS FOLLOW.

FIRST, EVERY BLOGVAULT SLOT IS REVENUE-BEARING. There is a paying client behind each one. No fixture, no test site, no internal clone ever consumes a slot. That is not a preference, it is displacing a customer. Fixtures go on the plain small server per m67921 and nowhere near BlogVault.

SECOND, AND THIS IS THE ONE: BEB-2124 MOVES 20 ROCKETNET SITES ONTO GRIDPANE, AND THE BACKUP PLAN IS AT 20 OF 20. If any of those 20 are markup clients expecting realtime backup, the migration lands them into an estate with zero backup capacity. That is a cost event and a client-promise event arriving together, and it is not in the ticket.

ANSWER THESE BEFORE THE MIGRATION RUNS, not after:
1. Of the 20 RocketNet sites, how many are on the 250% hosting markup and therefore carry a realtime backup expectation.
2. What GridPane's own backups actually give those sites — frequency, retention, and whether restore has ever been exercised. If GP backups are sufficient for this cohort, BlogVault does not need to grow at all and this evaporates.
3. If they are not sufficient, the price of the next BlogVault tier, set against the markup revenue those 20 sites carry. At a 250% markup the answer is probably that it pays for itself, but it should be a number rather than an assumption.

I am not filing a new ticket for this. It goes on BEB-2124 as a precondition, because a migration that silently drops a paid backup promise is worse than a migration that has not started.

DIRECTIVE 67923 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-2124, BEB-2126, BEB-2089 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

BEB-2124 IS MIS-SCOPED AND THE BACKUP COLLISION IN m67923 IS DEAD. Alex: RocketNet is MOSTLY DEV CLONES. ONE PAID SITE — a local ZZP-er's cake business. Not 20 client sites.

SO m67923 IS WITHDRAWN. Nineteen dev clones carry no backup promise and no markup. BlogVault does not need a tier, GridPane's backup adequacy does not need answering, and none of those three questions need work. Drop them.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE TICKET. It has sat blocked since 07-12 on BEB-2126, a RocketNet API credential, because enumerating and pulling 20 sites needs programmatic access. ONE site does not. WP Migrate runs from inside wp-admin on the source and we hold a LIFETIME licence. No API token, no vault row, no verb, no loop. The blocker that has held this ticket for eight weeks does not apply to the only site on it that matters.

I AM NOT CUTTING THE SCOPE — THAT IS ALEX'S ALONE. I am naming it: the ticket reads as a 20-site migration project and the actual content is one paid site plus nineteen dev clones that may not warrant moving at all. Whether those nineteen migrate, get archived, or get deleted is his call and I have put it to him.

WHAT TO DO NOW, WITHOUT WAITING FOR THAT CALL: the one paid site is the whole risk. It is a real business on a host we have lost SSH to. Get it off. wp-admin, WP Migrate, straight to a GridPane target, verified serving from the new host by a browser probe before anything on Rocket is touched. Nothing about that needs the loop, the credential, or a decision about the other nineteen.

CONFIRM ON THIS THREAD: does the cake site already hold a BlogVault slot, and does it sit on the 250% hosting markup. Those two answers decide what it needs on arrival and nothing else about this is blocked on them.
